title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Bertram (1) — Institution words improper; bread and wine exist FIGURATE; memory of Passion
pass_a_gloss: And (1) indeed, Bertram about to teach the impropriety of Christ’s Institution words: Bread and wine, he says, exist FIGURATIVELY as Christ’s body and blood. Likewise: This bread and cup, which are named the body and blood of Christ, represent the memory of the Lord’s Passion or death, just as He Himself said in the Gospel: Do this in remembrance of me. Which the Apostle Paul explaining says: as often as you shall have eaten the bread and drunk the cup, you will announce the Lord’s death until He come. We are taught by the Savior and also by S. Paul the Apostle that this bread and this blood, which are set upon the altar, are set in the FIGURE or memory of the Lord’s death, so that what was done in the past may recall present memory, that made mindful of His passion we may through it be made partakers of the divine gift through which we have been freed from death.
pass_b_english: Bertram (1): Institution words are improper — bread and wine exist FIGURATIVELY as Christ’s body and blood.

Named body and blood, they represent the memory of the Lord’s Passion; set on the altar in the FIGURE or memory of His death, so present memory of what was done may make us partakers of the divine gift.
source_text: Ac (1) quidem, verborum Institutionis Christi improprietatem edocturus Bertramus: Panis vinumque, ait ille, FIGURATE Christi corpus & sanguis existunt. Itemque: Iste panis & calix, qui corpus & sanguis Christi nominantur, memoriam representant Dominicæ Passionis sive mortis, quemadmodum ipse in Evangelio dixit: Hoc facite in meam commemorationem. Quod exponens Apostolus Paulus ait: quotiescunque manducaveritis panem & calicem biberitis, mortem Domini annunciabitis, donec veniat. Docemur à Salvatore nec non à S. Paulo Apostolo, quod iste panis & iste sanguis, qui super altare ponuntur, in FIGURAM sive memoriam Dominicæ mortis ponuntur, ut quod gestum est in præterito, præsenti revocet memoria, ut illius passionis memores effecti, per eam efficiamur divini muneris consortes, per quam sumus à morte liberati.
